newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-EDWARDS READY TO TAKE STEP INTO THE UNKNOWN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-EDWARDS READY TO TAKE STEP INTO THE UNKNOWN.

text.p: Jonathan Edwards concedes he will be taking "a step into the dark" when he starts the defence of his triple jump title at the world championships on Wednesday.
Edwards, 31, who set two world records on the way to winning the title in Gothenburg in 1995, has not competed for five weeks because of a heel injury.
"I wouldn't have come if I didn't think I could do myself justice," Edwards said on Tuesday.
"In some respects the qualifying competition tomorrow will be like taking a step in the dark. I did some jumps last week off a short run-up and didn't feel the injury.
"I am looking forward to competing and to defending my title which someone is going to have to fight very hard to take off me."
Edwards's main rival is Olympic champion Kenny Harrison of the United States.

"At our best I think Kenny and I are a little bit better than the rest, and I am looking forward to doing battle with him. But if we are anywhere below our best there are others who can catch us like the Cubans."
Although he has not jumped since the end of June, Edwards is currently ranked first in the world this season following his 17.74 metres at Munich on June 22.
Harrison's season's best came in Oslo on July 4 when he cleared 17.51, and Edwards believes it could take a big jump to clinch the gold.

"What's happened in the past, at Gothenburg and at Atlanta is irrelevant to today. Last year I think I lived in the shadow of what happened at Gothenburg. But now I am ready to write a new chapter in the story of my triple-jumping career."
